title: Custom Resources & CRDs
intro: Kubernetes lets you define entirely new resource types beyond the built-in ones (Pod, Deployment...). Operators and many add-ons work this way.

steps.prompt: List the CustomResourceDefinitions installed in the cluster.
steps.explanation: A CRD is what teaches the Kubernetes API about a new resource type — here, cert-manager registered a 'Certificate' kind.
steps.why: This is how you tell whether something like cert-manager or a database operator is actually installed — if its CRD isn't listed, its custom resources can't exist yet either.

steps.prompt: Get the full definition of the 'certificates.cert-manager.io' CRD.
steps.fake_output:
Name: certificates.cert-manager.io
Group: cert-manager.io
Kind: Certificate
Scope: Namespaced
steps.explanation: This tells you the Kind name ('Certificate') and API group you'd actually use to interact with resources of this new type.
steps.why: You need the Kind and group from here before you can run 'kubectl get certificates' — the CRD is effectively the schema registration, not a resource you work with directly day-to-day.

steps.prompt: Now list the actual custom resources of that new 'Certificate' kind.
steps.fake_output:
NAME          READY   SECRET        AGE
web-tls       True    web-tls-cert  4h
steps.explanation: Once the CRD exists, custom resources of that kind behave just like built-in ones — same get/describe/delete verbs work on them.
steps.why: This is the entire point of CRDs — 'kubectl get certificates' works identically to 'kubectl get pods' from a usage standpoint, even though Certificate isn't a resource Kubernetes ships with by default.

steps.prompt: See every resource type available under the cert-manager.io API group specifically.
steps.fake_output:
NAME           SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION            NAMESPACED   KIND
certificates   cert         cert-manager.io/v1   true         Certificate
steps.explanation: This scopes the api-resources list down to just one add-on's types instead of scrolling through every built-in resource too.
steps.why: Handy specifically after installing a new operator/CRD, to quickly see everything it just registered without the built-in Kubernetes types cluttering the list.
